title: The Money a Withdrawal Releases on a Keyturn Host Protection Plan Enrolment
content:
A host may take their own claim back off a Keyturn Host Protection Plan enrolment, and doing so releases money that stands booked as owed to them on the enrolment's claims.

### What is released

What a withdrawal releases is the whole of the money the claims on the enrolment have booked as owed to the host and not yet paid out, released in full with nothing retained for the standing of the enrolment, for how late the withdrawal comes, for claims on the enrolment that overlap the one being withdrawn or for the state of the reporting record, and rounded half up to two decimal places once, at the end.

### The figures each plan publishes

| Plan | Supplement window, calendar days | Claims allowed before review |
|---|---|---|
| Keyturn Shield 90 Host Plan | 14 | 2 |
| Keyturn Shield 85 Host Plan | 21 | 2 |
| Keyturn Shield 80 Host Plan | 30 | 3 |
| Keyturn Shield 75 Host Plan | 45 | 3 |
| Keyturn Shield 70 Host Plan | 60 | 4 |
| Keyturn Shield 60 Host Plan | 90 | 5 |

Every figure the plan publishes, its supplement window and the number of claims it allows before review among them, is read from the plan the enrolment is written on.

### Worked figure (hypothetical)

An enrolment whose claims have booked 4200 as owed to the host, and against which 1000 has already been paid out to them, has 3200 standing booked as owed and not yet paid out; a withdrawal on it releases 3200.00, the rounding half up to two decimal places being done once, at the end.
